intro.title: The Common Grounds Media Matrix
intro.text: A smooth, slide-based presentation comparing the two countries. It charts shared seafaring history, culinary crossovers and language links, and also covers family, faith, dress, crafts, architecture, music, celebrations and people.

ui.hint: Swipe, scroll or use the arrow keys

slides.title: Palms and Oases
slides.text: The palm is the tree of life in both countries. Bahrain was called the Island of a Million Palms and Tunisia's southern oases of Tozeur and Nefta shelter hundreds of thousands of palms. The palm gives dates, shade, rope, baskets, mats and fans. In 2019 the knowledge and traditions of the date palm were recognized by UNESCO as a shared heritage of Arab countries, including both Tunisia and Bahrain.
